text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali says parliamentary elections to be held next November as scheduled barring any unforseen circumstances; says temporary election law was necessary to accomodate administrative changes in constituencies.
- Majali says sees a turning point in U.S.-Iraqi ties, expresses optimism that Middle East peace process is passing through a crisis which it will surmount.
- Majali says government will focus on easing obstacles facing investment; Jordan calls on the U.S. to play the role of a real partner in the peace process.
- A group of parliamentarians proposing an increase in the number of parliamentary seats from the current 80-seat chamber.
- Saudi Foreign Minister visits Amman next month.
- Jordan warns of the dangers of Israel's possession of nuclear weapons in a memorandum sent to the International Atomic Agency (IAE).
- Prime Minister to meet heads of professional unions on Sunday to discuss union issues which are pending from the last government.
- Crown Prince calls on a delegation of U.S. investors to invest in trade and tourism; says opportunities are available in an improved business climate now prevailing in Jordan.
- Eight pro-government centrist parties close to reaching agreement on merger and choice of secretary general.
- Majali urges continued pressure on Israel; prime minister outlines results of king's U.S. talks; says Jordan wants quick end to Iraq sanctions.
